tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Add the bridge store, the binding bridge fields, and the three notice codes
tasks.description:
Implements spec §3.1 (durable bridge row + binding fields), §5.2 step 6 and §6.3 (external-ref table), §10.10 (unique indexes), §11.2 (schema-side additions). Acceptance criteria: A3.5, A10.6, A11.1, A11.2.

What to build:

1. Two new SQLite tables in `packages/db/src/schema/rooms.ts` (or a new `bridges.ts` in the same schema dir, exported from `packages/db/src/schema/index.ts`), with a generated Drizzle migration in `packages/db/drizzle/` — `pnpm --filter @dorkos/db db:check` must stay green (`scripts/assert-migrations-current.sh`).

   `room_bridges`:
   ```
   roomId              TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
   adapterId           TEXT NOT NULL
   chatId              TEXT NOT NULL
   channelType         TEXT               -- from the relay subject
   platformChatType    TEXT NOT NULL      -- 'private' | 'group' | 'supergroup'
   bindingId           TEXT NOT NULL
   visibility          TEXT               -- 'mentions-only' | 'everything' | null
   visibilityCheckedAt TEXT
   deliverNotices      INTEGER NOT NULL   -- seeded by room kind, see task 1.9
   lastDeliveredSeq    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
   lastActivityAt      TEXT
   createdAt           TEXT NOT NULL
   archivedAt          TEXT
   UNIQUE (adapterId, chatId)
   ```

   `room_bridge_messages` (the external-ref table; the ONLY echo-suppression mechanism in this feature — no text comparison, no time window, no recently-sent cache):
   ```
   roomId             TEXT NOT NULL
   entryId            TEXT NOT NULL
   direction          TEXT NOT NULL      -- 'inbound' | 'outbound'
   chatId             TEXT NOT NULL
   adapterId          TEXT NOT NULL
   platformMessageId  TEXT               -- nullable: outbound rows are written BEFORE the send
   threadId           TEXT               -- forum topic id (§5.6)
   threadName         TEXT               -- forum topic name, sanitized at write (§9.2)
   createdAt          TEXT NOT NULL
   ```
   Indexes: unique `(adapterId, chatId, platformMessageId)` where direction='inbound' (dedup lookup, §5.2 step 1); unique `(entryId)` (deliver idempotence, §6.3); index `(roomId, direction)`.

2. `apps/server/src/services/relay/chat-bridge/bridge-store.ts` — synchronous better-sqlite3 accessors: `createBridge`, `findBridgeByChat(adapterId, chatId)`, `findBridgeByRoom(roomId)`, `archiveBridge`, `unarchiveBridge`, `rebindBridge(bridgeId, bindingId)`, `stampActivity(bridgeId, at)`, `setLastDeliveredSeq`, `setVisibility`, `recordInboundRef`, `recordOutboundRef`, `patchOutboundPlatformId`, `findRefByEntry`, `findInboundRefByPlatformMessage`, `listUndeliveredAboveSeq(roomId, seq)`. Every write that must be atomic with a room write takes an optional transaction handle so task 1.6 can run steps 4-6 of §5.2 in one `better-sqlite3` transaction.

3. `AdapterBindingSchema` (`packages/shared/src/relay-adapter-schemas.ts:446`) gains:
   ```ts
   bridge: z.enum(['off', 'room']).default('off'),
   roomId: z.string().nullable().default(null),
   ```
   Add both to `UpdateBindingRequestSchema` as well or the cockpit cannot flip them. `bridge` defaulting to `'off'` IS the feature flag: no global flag, no `~/.dork/config.json` migration, every existing binding behaves exactly as today.

4. Validation at the schema/route boundary: a binding with `bridge: 'room'` MUST carry a `chatId`. A chat-wildcard binding (no `chatId`, which `BindingStore.resolve` treats as matching every chat on the adapter — `initiate-consent.ts:196-203`) cannot be bridged; the error message names the reason ("one room cannot honestly be the channel for an unbounded set of chats").

5. `RoomNoticeCodeSchema` (`packages/shared/src/room-schemas.ts:90`) gains exactly three codes: `bridge_blocked`, `bridge_undelivered`, `bridge_rate_limited`. This enum widening is the one non-additive change in the whole feature — a client pinned to the old enum fails to parse a room containing a bridge notice. It is a same-repo client shipped in lockstep, which is acceptable, but it must be called out explicitly in the OpenAPI diff review and in the changelog fragment.

Tests (all in `__tests__/` beside source):
- A3.5: `bridge: 'room'` with no `chatId` is rejected at the schema/route boundary with a message naming the wildcard reason.
- A10.6: a second bridge row for an occupied `roomId`, and a second for an occupied `(adapterId, chatId)`, are both rejected by the unique indexes (assert the constraint, not a guard clause).
- A11.2: a bindings-file fixture that predates this change (no `bridge` field) parses, defaults to `'off'`, and routes exactly as before.
- A11.1: OpenAPI regeneration is clean and the diff contains only additive fields except the `RoomNoticeCodeSchema` widening, which is enumerated in the review notes.
- bridge-store unit tests for every accessor, including that an outbound ref may be written with a null `platformMessageId` and patched afterward.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Add the four additive Telegram adapter fields and lift the captionless-media drop
tasks.description:
Implements spec §11.2 (the four adapter additions), §5.5 (non-text messages), §5.6 (forum topics), §6.8 (presence signal branch), §8 (privacy-mode source of truth). Acceptance criteria: A2.3, A5.7 (adapter half), A5.10 (adapter half), A6.8 (adapter half).

All four are additive payload fields or accessors. None changes the publish shape, the subject grammar `relay.human.{platform}.{instanceId}[.group].{chatId}` (`services/relay/human-subject.ts:36-63`), `RelayEnvelope`, `ChannelTypeSchema`, or `SignalTypeSchema`.

In `packages/relay/src/adapters/telegram/inbound.ts`:

1. `platformData.replyToMessageId` — the id of the message being replied to. Consumed by §5.4's reply-as-addressing (a reply to one of the agent's own messages counts as addressing it, matching Telegram's own privacy-mode semantics) and by §6.5's reply targeting.
2. `platformData.messageThreadId` AND `platformData.threadName` — the forum topic id and the topic NAME. The id so outbound delivery targets the right topic; the name so each entry can render a sanitized topic label. Both are needed: phase 1 folds all topics into one room (D-6 Q1), and a folded room without topic labels is an unreadable interleaving of several conversations.
3. `platformData.media` — a descriptor `{ type, durationSec?, fileName?, mimeType? }`, AND the lifting of the captionless-media drop at `inbound.ts:427-430`, which today returns early on `!rawText` so a captionless photo never publishes. The adapter emits descriptors only; it never authors placeholder prose — the placeholder string is built server-side in `ingest` (task 1.6) from these descriptors. No media bytes are downloaded, stored, or given to a model in phase 1.

In `packages/relay/src/adapters/telegram/telegram-adapter.ts`:

4. A `getMe` accessor exposing `can_read_all_group_messages` from the Bot API, so §8's visibility badge is sourced from the platform and never from config. Also expose `getMe().username`, which task 1.6 threads as an extra addressing candidate (Telegram addresses a bot as `@botusername`, which is not the agent's DorkOS handle).
5. The signal handler at `telegram-adapter.ts:341` branches only on `typing`; it gains a `'progress'` branch routing to the same `handleTypingSignal` (`outbound.ts:537`). `publishPresence` (`room-trigger.ts:214`) deliberately emits `progress`, not `typing` — agents work, they do not type (`specs/room-presence` §1). No new signal type, no second indicator.

Do NOT touch `shouldProcessGroupMessage` (`inbound.ts:235-244`) or `DEFAULT_RESPOND_MODE = 'thread-aware'` (`relay-adapter-schemas.ts:98`). That gate is load-bearing for §5.4 and must keep dropping unaddressed non-reply group messages BEFORE publish.

Tests:
- A2.3: with `respondMode` at its `'thread-aware'` default, an unaddressed group message produces no relay publish at all — asserted at the adapter, where the gate actually lives.
- A5.7 (adapter half): a captionless photo now publishes with a media descriptor and no text; a captioned one publishes with descriptor plus caption.
- A5.10 (adapter half): a forum-topic message publishes both `messageThreadId` and `threadName`.
- A6.8 (adapter half): a `progress` signal reaches `handleTypingSignal` and a released claim clears the indicator.
- Reply payload carries `replyToMessageId`.
- The grammY `Bot` boundary is the fake seam, matching existing adapter tests. Nothing mocks `RoomService`, `RoomTriggerDispatcher`, or the consent gate anywhere in this feature.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Create bridged rooms by bridge-row identity, never by member set
tasks.description:
Implements spec §3.2 (the single most important structural correction in this spec), §3.3 (kind mapping), §3.4 (roster and the atomic mention-only seed), §9.2 (sanitize at creation time). Founder rationale: `design-decisions.md` D-6 Q2 and D-7 amendment 1. Acceptance criteria: A3.2, A3.2b, A3.2c, A3.3, A3.4, A3.7, and the store half of A9.3.

The problem being fixed: `RoomStore.findDmByMemberSet` (`room-store.ts:197-218`) matches a DM by its exact member set, and `createRoom` consults it for every `kind: 'dm'` request (`room-service.ts:386-398`), returning and un-archiving the match. A bridged private chat whose roster is `{operator, bound agent}` is byte-identical to the operator's own private DM with that agent. Creating one naively would silently return the operator's existing private conversation, land strangers' messages in it, and make its private posts delivery candidates for a chat the operator never meant to expose.

Build:

1. `RoomService.createBridgedRoom(...)` — a dedicated create path that mints a room unconditionally, bypassing member-set matching. (A `dedupe: false` flag on `createRoom` is an acceptable alternative spelling; the property is what matters, the spelling is not — `design-decisions.md` "what this spec leaves to DECOMPOSE".) It writes the `room_bridges` row from task 1.1 in the same transaction as the room and its roster.
2. `findDmByMemberSet` gains `WHERE rooms.id NOT IN (SELECT room_id FROM room_bridges)` — enforced IN THE QUERY, not by convention at call sites, because a future caller will not know to avoid it.
3. Re-bridge resolution goes through the bridge store on `(adapterId, chatId)`, never through the roster. That natural key is what actually identifies this room, and it is what makes re-bridging idempotent.
4. Kind mapping, read from `platformData.chatType` (classified at `adapters/telegram/inbound.ts:349`) and stored as `platformChatType` so nothing re-derives it:
   - `private` → room kind `dm` (D-6 Q2; safe ONLY because of point 1 and 2 above)
   - `group` / `supergroup` → room kind `channel`, `channelType: 'group'` on the subject
   - `channel` (broadcast) → REFUSED. A broadcast channel is not a conversation.
   Recorded contingency: if the dedupe bypass proves invasive during implementation, the founder pre-approved falling back to kind `channel` for private chats — never a weakening of the §3.2 property. If you take the fallback, say so in the PR body; it cascades into task 1.9's `deliverNotices` seeding and task 1.15's "a DM has no badge" rule.
5. Roster at creation: the bound agent, plus the operator (local human author) so the person can speak into their own bridged chat from the cockpit without a join step, plus NO external humans (they are minted on first message, task 1.4). The bridge creates the room AS the operator author, so `requireOperator` on `addMember` (`room-service.ts:588-593`) and `requireSeedingAllowed` are satisfied by the person's own authority, never by an exemption.
6. **The `mention-only` seed cannot be a follow-up write.** `RoomRoster.seedResponseMode` returns `CHANNEL_RESPONSE_MODE = 'engaged'` for channels (`room-roster.ts:37, 208-212`), and `engaged` answers ordinary chatter inside a window — the exact over-participation D-3 forbids in a chat with strangers. A create-then-patch sequence leaves an observable window in which the agent is `engaged`. Pick implementation 1 of §3.4: `CreateRoomRequest` carries an optional per-member `responseMode`, resolved inside `createRoom`'s single transaction alongside `seedResponseMode`. (`RoomRoster.add` already takes `input.responseMode` and falls back to `seedResponseMode` only when the caller supplies none — `room-roster.ts:80` — so the plumbing exists.) ASSUMPTION LOGGED: option 1 is chosen over option 2 (flag-flip-last ordering) because A3.6b's agent-swap rebind in task 1.5 independently requires an atomic responseMode-in-add, so option 1 is the only choice that makes both paths use one mechanism. The invariant either way: there is no observable instant in which a bridged group room has a bound agent that is not `mention-only`.
7. Exactly one agent in the roster. A second is refused in phase 1 with a notice naming why (D-6 Q3: outbound consent is per binding, so a second agent's delivery has no gate that names it; `checkSender` would correctly deny it, producing a half-silent room where one agent answers into the chat and the other answers only into the cockpit).
8. Titles and slugs: a `dm` room's title is the external person's display name, sanitized; a `channel` room's title is the platform chat title, sanitized; its slug is `slugify(title)` and on collision with a live channel (`room-service.ts:348-353` throws `SLUG_TAKEN`) the bridge appends `-2`, `-3`, … until free. A platform title change does NOT rename an existing room (`room-service.ts:317-321`). Sanitization uses `sanitizeIdentity` from `@dorkos/shared/untrusted-text` — the existing function, never a second copy — applied at CREATION time as well as render time, because a platform title becomes a room title read by paths that predate this spec.

Tests:
- A3.2: bridging the same `(adapterId, chatId)` twice returns one room, resolved through the bridge store.
- A3.2b: bridging a private chat to an agent the operator already has a private DM with creates a second, distinct room; the operator's private DM is untouched — same id, same roster, same entry count, not un-archived, and never a delivery candidate.
- A3.2c: `findDmByMemberSet` never returns a bridged room — asserted directly against the query, with a bridged room whose member set exactly matches the requested one.
- A3.3: a bridged group room's bound agent is `mention-only` at every observable point, INCLUDING after a simulated failure of the second step of the chosen implementation.
- A3.4: a slug collision produces `#name-2`, never an error.
- A3.7: a broadcast-channel chat cannot be bridged.
- A9.3 (store half): a platform chat title containing markup is sanitized in the store, not only at render.
- Multi-agent refusal writes the notice naming the per-binding-consent reason.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Mint external authors, carry origin on the roster, and mark external entries in room context
tasks.description:
Implements spec §4.1-§4.4 (external member identity), §4.3 (origin), §9.2 (the three regions, the `authorOrigin` marking, the bridged-room standing line). Acceptance criteria: A4.1, A4.2, A4.3, A4.4, A4.5, A4.6, A9.2, A9.4, A9.5.

1. **Natural key.** `AuthorRegistry.resolve({kind, naturalKey, displayName})` (`services/rooms/author-registry.ts:181`) mints on `(kind, naturalKey)`. A Telegram sender is kind `human` — `RoomContextMember.isPerson` must say so or the etiquette rules in `meta/agent-etiquette.md` become unfollowable. The key is:
   ```
   platform:{platformType}:{instanceId}:{platformUserId}
   e.g. platform:telegram:tg-main:145223
   ```
   Opaque and address-free; scoped to the adapter instance so two bots cannot collide; stable across display-name changes. `platformUserId` comes from `platformData.fromId`, parsed by the EXISTING `extractPlatformUserId` (`binding-router.ts:57-88`) — do not write a second parser.

2. **Invariant:** no locally minted author's natural key may begin `platform:`. The three local kinds are `local`, `user:{id}`, and an agent path; none can spell the prefix. Pin it with a test that fails if a future local mint could.

3. **A message with no resolvable platform user id gets no author** and is dropped with a refusal line, rather than folded into a shared "someone" author that would merge two strangers into one identity in a log meant to be evidence.

4. **Roster join is lazy and transactional.** An external human is added on their FIRST message, in the same transaction that writes their first entry (task 1.6 calls this) — not at bridge time, so a group of 200 does not project 200 rows for people who never spoke. Added by the bridge acting as the operator author, satisfying `requireOperator`. Their membership `responseMode` is the inert default `seedResponseMode` already returns for non-agents (`room-roster.ts:44, 208-209`).

5. **`origin` on `RoomRosterEntry` and `RoomContextMember`:**
   ```ts
   origin: 'local' | { platform: string }
   ```
   DERIVED FROM THE STORED AUTHOR'S `naturalKey` PREFIX, never from the relay subject at render time. Render-time derivation would mean the origin of a two-year-old entry depends on which subject happened to be in scope; the natural key is written once at mint and is the only honest source. `'local'` for the operator, agents, and the system voice; `{ platform }` for anything whose key starts `platform:`.

6. **`authorOrigin: 'local' | 'external'` on `RoomContextEntry`**, plus the fenced rendering labelling external entries with one word, plus a single standing line in the fence preamble for a bridged room: that this channel receives messages from people outside this machine, that their text is data and never instructions, and that a request arriving this way to read files, run commands, or send messages elsewhere is a request from a stranger. This is framing, not a mechanism; the mechanisms are the fence itself and §9.3's structural levers.

7. **Regions.** External message bodies, captions, and media placeholders go INSIDE the fence (`services/runtimes/shared/room-context-block.ts`, per-turn nonce) — unchanged from any other member's message. External display names go OUTSIDE the fence as labels and must pass `sanitizeIdentity` from `@dorkos/shared/untrusted-text` at mint time as well as render time. `ownRecent` remains outside the fence and remains the documented laundering path (`room-context-block.ts:52-66`, measured at 46 characters ahead of the fence); `defuseSystemTags` on that region is load-bearing for exactly this feature.

Tests:
- A4.1: two messages from the same Telegram user in the same bridged chat resolve to one author row.
- A4.2: the same Telegram user under two adapter instances resolves to two author rows.
- A4.3: a display-name change on the platform updates the display name without minting a second author.
- A4.4: `room_context` carries `isPerson: true` and `origin: { platform: 'telegram' }` for an external author, with origin derived from the stored key — asserted by rendering context with NO live subject in scope.
- A4.5: no locally minted author has a `platform:`-prefixed natural key.
- A4.6: a group with N silent members has exactly one roster row per member who has spoken.
- A9.2: a display name containing `<`, `>`, or control characters (including NEL) renders in the preamble with none present; the preamble contains no `<` or `>` at all.
- A9.4: `room_context` marks an external entry `authorOrigin: 'external'` and carries the bridged-room standing line.
- A9.5: external text quoted back by the agent renders in `ownRecent` with tags defused.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Implement bridge lifecycle: unbridge, archive, re-bridge, and the agent-swap rebind
tasks.description:
Implements spec §3.5 (unbinding and archival, all six rows of the table), §10.9 (room archived out-of-band). Founder rationale: `design-decisions.md` D-7 amendment 1. Acceptance criteria: A3.6, A3.6b, A10.5.

Archive is the only removal. The room log is never trimmed (ADR `260726-170125`).

Behaviours to implement, each with the notice it posts:

1. **Bridge switched `room` → `off`:** room ARCHIVED; a notice records that the chat is no longer connected; `binding.roomId` cleared. The bridge row and EVERY external ref survive — only `binding.bridge` flips and `archivedAt` is stamped. This is what keeps echo suppression and reply targeting working across a re-bridge.
2. **Binding deleted:** same.
3. **Bot blocked / kicked (§10.3):** same, with the platform's own reason in the notice.
4. **Re-bridged for the same `(adapterId, chatId)`, same agent:** the surviving bridge row is found, its room UN-ARCHIVED and reused, `archivedAt` cleared.
5. **Re-bridged for the same `(adapterId, chatId)`, a DIFFERENT agent:** the surviving row's `UNIQUE (adapterId, chatId)` makes a second row impossible, and that is the right answer rather than an obstacle. The rebind ADOPTS the surviving bridge row and its room: re-point `bindingId`, swap the roster's bound agent. The room IS the chat's history, and minting a parallel room would strand it — the same reasoning `createRoom` applies to a re-opened DM (`room-service.ts:314-318`). Three consequences, ALL stated in one notice posted into the room at the swap: (a) the new agent inherits the full room log as ambient history and reads every prior message, including the old agent's; (b) the old agent leaves the roster and its `(room, agent)` session is dropped from the ledger, so its private transcript is orphaned rather than migrated; (c) the room keeps its id, title, slug and every external ref, so echo suppression and reply targeting stay continuous. A person who wants a clean start un-bridges, archives the room, and bridges fresh — the destructive option stays explicit.
   On a bridged CHANNEL the swapped-in agent must be `mention-only` at every observable point — the same invariant task 1.3 sets at creation, held for the same reason: `RoomRoster.add` takes `input.responseMode` and falls back to `seedResponseMode` only when the caller supplies none (`room-roster.ts:80`), so the swap path seeds the mode ATOMICALLY IN THE ADD, never as a follow-up patch.
6. **Agent unregistered from the mesh:** room stays; the existing `agent_gone` notice path reports it. No new behaviour — do not add one.
7. **§10.9 archived out-of-band:** `RoomService.post` throws `ROOM_ARCHIVED` (`room-service.ts:696`); the ingest path catches it, sets `bridge: 'off'`, and tells the chat ONCE through the existing `chatNotice` path.

All notices are written through `room-notice-log.ts` (the single writer) and damped.

Tests:
- A3.6: un-bridging archives and preserves the bridge row and refs; re-bridging to the SAME agent un-archives the same room id and appends to the same log.
- A3.6b: re-bridging the same `(adapterId, chatId)` to a DIFFERENT agent adopts the surviving bridge row and its room — same room id, roster's bound agent swapped, old agent's ledger entry dropped, external refs intact, one notice naming the swap; the swapped-in agent is `mention-only` at every observable point, asserted after a simulated failure of any step FOLLOWING the add.
- A10.5: posting into an archived bridged room turns the bridge off exactly once and notifies the chat once (assert the damping, not just the first call).
- Bot-blocked (403) archival writes the platform's reason into the notice.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Add ChatBridge.ingest as the terminal branch in BindingRouter
tasks.description:
Implements spec §5.1-§5.6 (the whole inbound flow), §7.2 (`sessionMap` is not consulted for a bridged binding), §14 (per-chat serialization). Acceptance criteria: A2.1, A2.2, A5.1, A5.2, A5.3, A5.4, A5.5, A5.6, A5.7 (server half), A5.8, A5.9, A5.10 (server half), A7.3.

Code lives at `apps/server/src/services/relay/chat-bridge/` — `ingest.ts`, `catch-up.ts`, `index.ts` (with `bridge-store.ts` from task 1.1 and `deliver.ts` from task 1.8).

**The routing change** in `BindingRouter.handleInbound` (`apps/server/src/services/relay/binding-router.ts:379`), after the existing binding resolve at `:426` (enabled / canReceive / agent-in-mesh checks unchanged):
```
if (binding.bridge === 'room') → ChatBridge.ingest(binding, envelope)   ← NEW, TERMINAL
else                          → resolveSession → publish relay.agent.…  ← unchanged
```
`ingest` is TERMINAL. Falling through would run the turn twice from one message.

**What `ingest` does, in order:**
1. **Dedup** on `{adapterId, chatId, platformMessageId}` from `platformData.messageId`. An existing inbound ref stops here: refusal reason `duplicate_inbound`, no entry, no notice, no turn. Telegram redelivers on webhook retry and on a polling/webhook overlap during restart, so this is a routine path, not an edge case.
2. **Rate ceiling** — a per-`(adapterId, chatId)` rolling inbound count over a short window. Past it, `ingest` REFUSES with a damped `bridge_rate_limited` notice in the room and writes nothing. Refusing, not trimming: a trim policy would undermine the log's whole purpose. ASSUMPTION TO LOG: the spec fixes the shape but not the numbers; start at 60 accepted messages per chat per 60s rolling window, as a named exported constant so it is one edit to change.
3. **Resolve the room** from the bridge row. A `bridge: 'room'` binding whose room is missing is a broken bridge: log a refusal, tell the person in-chat through the existing `chatNotice` path, and DO NOT create a room — a bridge whose room the person archived out-of-band must not resurrect itself.
4. **Resolve or mint the external author** (task 1.4); add them to the roster if new.
5. **Write the entry** through `RoomService.post` as that author. `post` resolves addressing at write time (`room-service.ts:718`), appends, publishes (`:740`), and dispatches inside a `try` so a committed post is never lost to a dispatch failure (`:754-770`). The bridge does nothing else — **the bridge writes a post and stops; it never triggers a turn.** Every decision about whether an agent answers stays in `addressing.ts`, `cascade-guard.ts`, `turn-budget.ts`, and `RoomTriggerDispatcher`.
6. **Record the inbound external ref** — `(roomId, entryId, direction: 'inbound', chatId, platformMessageId, threadId?, threadName?)` — in the SAME transaction as step 5. Steps 4-6 run in one SQLite transaction; `better-sqlite3` is synchronous, so that is a real transaction.

Also stamp `bridge.lastActivityAt` on every accepted ingest (consumed by task 1.12's notify-target recency).

**Ordering (§5.3):** the room log's `seq` is the order the bridge ACCEPTED messages, not the platform's clock. `ingest` is serialized per `(adapterId, chatId)` by an in-process promise chain so two updates cannot interleave their transactions. Nothing reorders on platform timestamps: a log that silently reorders is worse evidence than one that is honestly append-only. This serializes ingest — a few indexed writes — and never serializes turns.

**Media placeholders (§5.5):** build the placeholder text SERVER-SIDE from task 1.2's `platformData.media` descriptors — `[photo]`, `[voice message, 0:14]`, `[document: report.pdf]` — plus any caption, with the caption inside the same untrusted region as any other message text. Never from adapter-authored prose.

**Mention translation (§5.4):** Telegram addresses a bot as `@botusername`, which is not the agent's DorkOS handle. `ingest` REWRITES NOTHING — the log holds exactly what the person typed. Instead thread ONE extra addressing candidate for the bound agent in that room, from `getMe().username` (task 1.2), through the existing chain: `RoomRoster.addressingCandidates` (`room-roster.ts:183`) → `rosterMentionCandidates` → `claimNames` (`author-handles.ts:161`). `claimNames` is first-claimant-wins, so the extra candidate is APPENDED after the agent's own advertised handles and can never steal a name another member already claims.

Tests:
- A2.1 / A5.2: a bridged binding never reaches session dispatch — asserted with a SPY ON THE SESSION CREATOR (`AgentSessionCreator`), not by reading code order.
- A2.2: a bridged room's turn goes through `RoomTriggerDispatcher`, asserted by OBSERVING A TURN CLAIM, not a runtime call.
- A5.1: the same platform message id ingested twice produces one entry and one turn.
- A5.3: two concurrent inbound messages produce two entries with `seq` in acceptance order and no interleaved partial state.
- A5.4: in a bridged group with privacy mode OFF and `respondMode: 'always'`, an unmentioned message writes an entry, triggers no turn, and appears in the next triggered turn's `room_context` as an unread entry. tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Add the server-only relay.bridge principal, the gate's one non-exempt branch, and the provenance classifier
tasks.description:
Implements spec §6.4 (the delivery principal and `isServerOnlyPrincipal`), §6.6 (consent: reply vs initiate, and what actually enforces it), §9.3, §11.1, §11.2. Founder rationale: `design-decisions.md` D-7 amendments 2, 3, and 4 — which are ONE decision and must not be separated. Acceptance criteria: A6.4 (gate half), A6.5 (the author-check helper), A6.10, A9.7, A11.3, and the ten-case consent table in §13.

**THIS TASK MUST MERGE BEFORE TASK 1.8.** `relay.bridge.*` is deliberately non-exempt so the gate evaluates it; but non-exempt is not the same as unassertable. `POST /api/relay/messages` rejects a client-supplied `from` only when `isConsentExemptPrincipal(from)` is true (`apps/server/src/routes/relay.ts:202`), so a non-exempt principal sails through — and with `canReply` defaulting to `true` (`relay-adapter-schemas.ts:475`), any local caller could publish arbitrary text into the chat AS THE BOT, with no room entry and no external ref. If task 1.8 lands first, `main` carries that hole for the length of the gap.

**The honest starting point: `canReply` is unenforced today.** `bindingAllowsInitiate` is `enabled && canInitiate` (`initiate-consent.ts:134-136`); replies ride the blanket `agent:*` exemption (`:157`); `canReply` is read only into `__bindingPermissions` alongside `permissionMode`. This feature has to enforce it.

Build, in `apps/server/src/services/relay/`:

1. **The principal grammar** `relay.bridge.{reply|initiate}.{adapterId}.{chatId}`, with a parser. The classification sits AHEAD of the variable-length tail because a Telegram chat id — and, later, a Slack channel id — may contain a dot: parsing from a fixed position after the `relay.bridge.` prefix cannot be shifted by anything in `adapterId` or `chatId`. Putting it at the end would make the gate's read depend on how many dots the chat id happened to have, the class of bug `parseHumanSubject` was written carefully to avoid (`human-subject.ts:55-60`).
2. **`isServerOnlyPrincipal(from) = isConsentExemptPrincipal(from) || from.startsWith('relay.bridge.')`**, beside `isConsentExemptPrincipal` in `services/relay/initiate-consent.ts`, and used by `routes/relay.ts:202` ONLY. It answers "a client may not assert this", which is a DIFFERENT question from "the consent gate trusts this". `isConsentExemptPrincipal` keeps exactly its three branches and its one meaning. The two predicates living side by side, with the wider one named for what it actually guards, IS the point — collapsing them is how this hole opened in the first place. The route returns 403.
3. **One new NON-EXEMPT branch in `createInitiateConsentGate`** (`initiate-consent.ts:208`) for `relay.bridge.*` principals, which: (a) reads the classification from the principal's fixed third segment, DENYING an unrecognised value rather than defaulting to either; (b) parses `{adapterId, chatId}` from the target subject and resolves the binding, denying `NO_BINDING` if none; (c) enforces `binding.enabled && binding.canReply` for an asserted reply, and `bindingAllowsInitiate(binding)` (i.e. `enabled && canInitiate`) for an asserted initiate. The exempt set is UNCHANGED — this is an extension of enforcement, not a widening of exemption.
4. **A provenance classifier as a pure, testable module** consumed by `deliver` in task 1.8. `InitiateConsentGate` is `(from, subject) => decision` (`packages/relay/src/types.ts:169`) — two strings. It cannot see the entry, its `cascadeRoot`, the external-ref table, or the delivering author, so classification CANNOT live there. The classifier takes the entry, the bridge row, and the ref table and answers:
   > An entry is a **reply** if and only if its `cascadeRoot` names an entry IN THE SAME ROOM that carries an INBOUND external ref for the SAME `(adapterId, chatId)`. Everything else is an **initiate**.
   The room scoping is load-bearing: `activeTurnFor` → `deepestClaimOf` (`room-claims.ts:212-224`) picks the deepest live claim for an author ACROSS EVERY ROOM, so an agent triggered in bridged chat R that also posts into bridged chat S would inherit R's cascade root — and R's root is an inbound platform entry. Without the same-room-same-chat condition, a stranger's mention in R launders an initiate into S straight past `canInitiate: false`.
5. **A delivering-author check helper**, also consumed by `deliver`: the author must be the binding's agent or the operator. §9.3's "an agent cannot deliver to a chat it is not bound to" rests HERE, not on `checkSender` (`initiate-consent.ts:260-303`), which never sees a bridge delivery's author.
6. **`bridge_blocked` notice copy**, written through `room-notice-log.ts` (the single writer) and damped per `(room, reason)`. The copy names the switch and where it lives. Plus the dedicated restart copy: turn claims are memory-only, so a late answer posted after a restart has no live claim, `post` self-roots it (`deriveCascade` at `room-service.ts:729`), and it classifies as an INITIATE — fail-closed silence on a chat with `canInitiate: false`. That is the right failure direction and the wrong experience to leave unexplained:
   > "This answer lost its provenance — the server restarted mid-turn — and was treated as a new conversation. It stayed here."

**Trusting the caller's asserted classification is safe for exactly one reason: `relay.bridge.*` is server-only.** The route guard and the gate branch are one decision; do not ship either alone.

Tests — this task owns the §13 centrepiece, the ten-case consent table (cases 1-7 and 9-10 here; case 8 is the author-check helper, exercised end-to-end in task 1.8):
1. inbound root, same room/chat, `canReply: true` → delivered
2. same, `canReply: false` → blocked + notice (the test that would have passed vacuously before this spec)
3. cockpit post, `canInitiate: true` → delivered
4. cockpit post, `canInitiate: false` → blocked + notice
5. scheduled task, `canInitiate: true` → delivered
6. scheduled task, `canInitiate: false` → blocked + notice
7. inbound root, binding paused (`enabled: false`), any → blocked
9. CROSS-ROOM LEAK: agent triggered in bridged chat R posts into bridged chat S whose binding has `canInitiate: false` → BLOCKED
10. POST-RESTART: late answer with no live claim, self-rooted, chat has `canInitiate: false` → blocked, with the dedicated restart copy
Plus:
- A6.10: a client-asserted `relay.bridge.*` principal on `POST /api/relay/messages` is rejected 403 by `isServerOnlyPrincipal`, and the three previously reserved principals are still rejected by the same route.
- A11.3 / §13 unit: `isServerOnlyPrincipal` accepts the three exempt principals plus `relay.bridge.*` and rejects `relay.human.console` and `relay.agent.*`; a PAIRED test asserts `isConsentExemptPrincipal` still answers `false` for `relay.bridge.*`, so the two predicates cannot be collapsed by a later edit. The gate has exactly one new non-exempt branch.
- Principal parse with a chat id CONTAINING A DOT, both spellings.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Implement log-driven delivery with write-before-send echo suppression and the failure ladder
tasks.description:
Implements spec §6.1 (what delivers and what drives delivery), §6.3 (echo suppression and write-before-send ordering), §6.5 (reply targeting and threading), §6.7 (author prefixing), §10.1-§10.4, §10.7, §10.8. Acceptance criteria: A6.1, A6.2, A6.3, A6.4 (delivery half), A6.5, A6.7, A6.9, A10.1, A10.2, A10.3, A10.4, A10.7, A12.1.

Merges AFTER task 1.7 — this is the first code that asserts a `relay.bridge.*` principal, and the route guard that makes that principal unassertable by a client must already be on `main`.

`apps/server/src/services/relay/chat-bridge/deliver.ts` + `catch-up.ts`.

**Eligibility.** A committed room entry is delivered when ALL of these hold: (1) the room has a live bridge; (2) `kind` is `post`, OR it is a `notice` this bridge's `deliverNotices` setting makes eligible (task 1.9 owns that clause's defaults; wire the hook here); (3) the entry has no `direction: 'inbound'` external ref; (4) the author is the bound agent or the operator; (5) the consent check from task 1.7 passes.

**Delivery is driven off the durable room log, never off the live stream.** `publishEntry` → `RoomBroadcaster` (`room-stream.ts:40`) is a live fan-out that DROPS events for absent subscribers, so a bridge subscribed to it would silently lose every entry committed while the adapter was down or reconnecting. Instead: the bridge attempts delivery inline on commit (the fast path), and keeps `lastDeliveredSeq` on the bridge row; on start, on adapter reconnect, and after a delivery failure resolves, it SCANS the bridged room for entries above `lastDeliveredSeq` that qualify under criteria 1-5 and lack an outbound ref, and delivers them in `seq` order. **The scan applies the same eligibility test as the inline path, including criterion 2's notice clause** — scoping the scan to `kind: 'post'` would mean a `turn_failed` committed while the adapter was down never catches up, so the one notice a bridged DM exists to deliver would be the one notice that silently never arrives. The scan is the authority; the inline attempt is an optimization. FLAG FOR EXECUTE: the spec names three scan triggers but the codebase has no enumerated "adapter reconnected" or "failure resolved" event — resolve this by hooking `AdapterManager`'s existing lifecycle and a bounded retry-completion callback, and say in the PR which hooks you used.

**Echo suppression** is the external-ref table and nothing else — structural, never heuristic; no text comparison, no time window, no recently-sent cache. An entry written by `ingest` carries an `inbound` ref and `deliver` skips it. `deliver` WRITES ITS `outbound` REF BEFORE CALLING THE PLATFORM, with a null platform message id, and patches the id in after the send returns. A crash between write and send therefore yields a SUPPRESSED RETRY (an entry that looks delivered and is not) rather than a DUPLICATE (a message a person sees twice). That is the correct side to fail on: a missing message is visible in the room and recoverable by the person; a duplicate in someone else's chat is not recallable. A row whose platform id is still null after the retry budget is resolved by §10.1's notice, so the suppressed case is never silent. `deliver` is idempotent on `entryId`: an existing outbound row is a no-op.

**Consent wiring.** `deliver` holds the entry, the bridge row, and the refs, so it: (1) calls task 1.7's classifier for reply-vs-initiate; (2) runs task 1.7's delivering-author check BEFORE any publish; (3) publishes to the chat's `relay.human.*` subject through `RelayCore.publish` under `relay.bridge.reply.{adapterId}.{chatId}` or `relay.bridge.initiate.{adapterId}.{chatId}`.

**Reply targeting (§6.5).** For a delivered entry whose provenance resolves to an inbound entry, set `reply_to_message_id` to that message's platform id and `message_thread_id` to the inbound ref's topic id when present. For an entry answering nothing, set neither.

**Author prefixing (§6.7).** Any delivered post whose author is not the bound agent — in practice the operator posting from the cockpit — is prefixed with that author's display name AT DELIVERY TIME ONLY. The prefix is NEVER written into the entry body: the log holds exactly what the person typed, and a stored prefix would be re-applied on every re-delivery and corrupt the record. The reason it exists at all: the bot is the only identity Telegram gives us, so without the prefix a person in the group cannot tell the operator speaking from the agent speaking.

**Failure ladder.**
- 10.1 platform down / adapter disconnected: sends fail with the ref already written; retry with bounded backoff (3 attempts, exponential, ≤ 2 min). On final failure the room gets a damped `bridge_undelivered` notice naming the entry, and the ref's null platform id makes the entry eligible for the catch-up scan when the adapter returns.
- 10.2 rate limit (429 + `retry_after`): honour `retry_after` exactly; deliveries for that chat queue behind it in `seq` order. Sustained limiting past the retry budget degrades to 10.1.
- 10.3 bot blocked / kicked / chat deleted (403): TERMINAL, not retried — hand to task 1.5's archival path with the platform's reason.
- 10.4 late replies: reused unchanged. Late delivery posts the answer into the room with how long it took (`room-trigger.ts:983+`); the bridge delivers that post like any other.

Stamp `bridge.lastActivityAt` on successful delivery (task 1.12 consumes it).

Tests:
- A6.1: an inbound message never round-trips back to the platform.
- A6.2: a `deliver` retry for an already-delivered entry sends nothing; a crash between ref-write and send yields no duplicate on retry.
- A6.3: a cockpit-authored post reaches the chat when `canInitiate` is on and does not when off; the off case writes `bridge_blocked`.
- A6.4 (delivery half): an agent's answer to a platform message reaches the chat with `canInitiate` OFF and `canReply` ON, and does NOT with `canReply` off. Companion test reads the `from` string off the publish and asserts `relay.bridge.reply.…` for the answer and `relay.bridge.initiate.…` for a cockpit post, WITH A CHAT ID CONTAINING A DOT, so a positional parse error cannot hide behind a passing gate decision.
- A6.5 (consent table case 8): a bridge delivery whose author is not the binding's agent or the operator is refused INSIDE `deliver`, before any publish — asserted by observing NO PUBLISH, not by observing a gate decision.
- A6.7: a delivered answer to a forum-topic message carries that topic's `message_thread_id`.
- A6.9: an operator-authored delivered post carries the display-name prefix ON THE WIRE and NOT in the stored entry body.
- A10.1, A10.2, A10.3, A10.4 per the ladder above, including that a 429 preserves `seq` order.
- A10.7: an entry committed while the adapter is down is delivered after reconnect EXACTLY ONCE, driven by the catch-up scan with a SUBSCRIBER DROP SIMULATED so the live stream cannot be what carried it. Sibling case asserts the same for a `deliverNotices`-eligible `turn_failed`, which a `kind: 'post'`-scoped scan would have stranded.
- A12.1: with no bridge enabled anywhere, the full existing relay test suite passes unchanged.
- Integration: full inbound→room→turn→outbound with `FakeAgentRuntime` and a fake Telegram transport faked at the grammY `Bot` boundary. Nothing mocks `RoomService`, `RoomTriggerDispatcher`, or the consent gate — a mock of those would encode the hypothesis instead of testing it (`.claude/rules/testing.md`).

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Key deliverNotices on room kind, with one per-bridge override
tasks.description:
Implements spec §6.2 (notices). Founder rationale: `design-decisions.md` D-6 Q5 — the answer is keyed on who is standing on the other end. Acceptance criterion: A6.6, plus the notice half of A10.7.

Room notices (`cascade_stopped`, `budget_reached`, `agent_busy`, `turn_failed`, `agent_gone`, `awaiting_approval`, `halted`) are cockpit-shaped, and two would actively leak: `agent_busy` deliberately says nothing about where, and `agent_gone` names an agent the platform person has no relationship with.

Build:
1. `deliverNotices` is a per-bridge boolean SEEDED BY ROOM KIND at bridge creation: `true` for a bridged `dm`, `false` for a bridged `channel`. A bridged DM is usually the operator's own account, and silence after a crashed turn is exactly the failure `.claude/rules/room-conduct.md` exists to prevent; a bridged group is other people, who do not need this machine's internals.
2. Exactly ONE per-bridge override, exposed on the bridge/binding update route and surfaced in task 1.14's UI.
3. Scope when on is EXACTLY `turn_failed` and `halted` — not the other five — rendered as one plain sentence each, written for a person on Telegram, not a cockpit reader (`writing-for-humans`).
4. Wire this as criterion 2 of task 1.8's eligibility test, used identically by the inline path AND the catch-up scan.
5. Final copy for all three new codes: `bridge_blocked` (task 1.7 owns its two variants), `bridge_undelivered`, `bridge_rate_limited` — all through `room-notice-log.ts`, all damped.

Note: if task 1.3 took the recorded D-6 Q2 fallback (bridged private chats get kind `channel` instead of `dm`), the seeding rule must key on `platformChatType` from the bridge row rather than on room kind, or every bridged DM silently loses its `turn_failed` notice. Check which way 1.3 landed before implementing.

Tests:
- A6.6: a room notice does not reach the chat from a bridged `channel` by default; `turn_failed` DOES from a bridged `dm` by default.
- The per-bridge override flips each case, and only `turn_failed` and `halted` are ever eligible — assert the other five are not, individually.
- A10.7 sibling: a `deliverNotices`-eligible `turn_failed` committed while the adapter was down is caught up by the scan.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Forward room presence to the chat as a Telegram typing action

Implements spec §6.8 (presence). Acceptance criterion: A6.8.

The bridge is the missing publisher that `packages/relay/src/adapters/telegram/outbound.ts:527-529` describes in its own words: "No such bridge exists yet: room presence is published to the room's own event stream (`RoomService.publishSignal`) and reaches the cockpit, not a relay adapter." `.claude/rules/room-conduct.md` lists it as the one remaining known gap; this task closes it.

Task 1.2 gave the Telegram adapter's signal handler (`telegram-adapter.ts:341`) a `'progress'` branch routing to the same `handleTypingSignal` (`outbound.ts:537`). This task adds the bridge-side forwarder: for a bridged room, a presence signal becomes a relay signal on the chat's `relay.human.*` subject. No new signal type, no second indicator.

The honesty property is unchanged and must be preserved: the indicator exists exactly as long as the turn claim, and releasing the claim clears it.

Note the deliberate asymmetry with §6.1: entry DELIVERY is driven off the durable log because a dropped live-stream event is a lost message, but PRESENCE is ephemeral by nature and riding the live signal stream is correct for it. State that in a comment so a future reader does not "fix" it into the durable path.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Adopt an existing session at bridge time, gated on a real transcript probe
tasks.description:
Implements spec §7.1-§7.4 (history semantics and the migration off `sessionMap`). Acceptance criteria: A7.1, A7.2, A7.4.

Bridging a binding that already has a live session MAY adopt it as the room's `(room, agent)` session. Adoption is attractive — a person who bridges a week-old chat should not have their agent forget the week — but it is not safe unconditionally, because `BindingRouter` is NOT an `onProjectorRekey` listener (`apps/server/src/index.ts:1289` registers only the connector service), so a session id in `sessions.json` can name a session that was rekeyed out from under it.

The rule:
1. Find THE SINGLE `{bindingId}:chat:{chatId}` entry, whatever the `sessionStrategy` — the key is what identifies the conversation, not the strategy label. More than one candidate, or none: start fresh.
2. **Probe that the session has a real transcript**, plus a matching runtime type. USE THE EXISTING READER — DO NOT WRITE A SECOND ONE: `TranscriptReader.hasTranscript(vaultRoot, sessionId) → { exists, root? }` (`services/runtimes/claude-code/sessions/transcript-reader.ts:207-213`), which searches across accounts and returns the owning account root when it finds one. That is the DURABLE signal — the JSONL file on disk, the fact `hasStarted` names (`agent-types.ts:49`: "True once the first SDK query has been sent (JSONL file exists)"). It must NOT read the in-process session map (`sessions/session-store.ts:221`), which is empty after a restart and would make adoption fail for every bridge created shortly after the app launches — precisely when a person is most likely to be setting one up. A stale or never-started id fails the probe.
3. Probe passes → write it into the room-session ledger for `(room, boundAgent)`, remove it from `sessionMap`, persist, and post a notice: the conversation continues here, and the earlier messages live in that session.
4. Probe fails → start fresh, and post the same notice minus the pointer.

**The room log does NOT gain the old messages.** Telegram gives bots no history read, and the session transcript is runtime-owned (ADR-0310); copying it into the room would be DorkOS asserting a record it did not witness. The notice says exactly this, in plain words.

§7.2: for a binding with `bridge: 'room'`, `sessionMap` is not consulted and not written. `sessionStrategy` becomes meaningless for that binding — the UI hides it with a line explaining that a bridged chat keeps its history in the channel (task 1.14). The field is NOT removed: unbridged bindings still use it and the wire format does not change.

§7.4: unbridging does not return the session to `sessionMap`. The room keeps it; a re-bridged chat re-adopts it from the ledger. A chat that goes back to private-pipe mode starts a new session, and the archived room's notice says where the old one went.

FLAG FOR EXECUTE: `hasTranscript` is claude-code-specific, but a binding's agent may run on codex or opencode (ADR-0309, ADR-0308), whose session storage is runtime-owned and has no equivalent probe. Implement the probe behind a per-runtime capability check: claude-code probes, other runtimes fail the probe and start fresh with the pointer-less notice. Do not fabricate a probe for a runtime that cannot answer it.

Tests:
- A7.1: after bridging a binding with a live, started session, THE FIRST TURN IN THE BRIDGED ROOM RESUMES THAT CONVERSATION — asserted on the runtime's resumed conversation (the transcript the turn receives), not on the ledger row.
- A7.2: bridging a binding whose `sessionMap` id fails the transcript probe starts fresh and posts the pointer-less notice.
- A7.4: a turn in a bridged room receives `room_context` containing the prior room entries.
- Integration with a `sessions.json` fixture, probe-pass and probe-fail.
- A codex- or opencode-backed binding takes the fresh-start path without error.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Make resolveNotifyTarget bridge-aware so proactive notifications survive the sessionMap vacate
tasks.description:
Implements spec §7.5 (proactive notifications must not die with `sessionMap`). Acceptance criterion: A7.5.

This is a regression guard, and the regression it guards is invisible until someone notices their agent stopped telling them things. `resolveNotifyTarget`'s `pickMostRecentChat` walks `bindingRouter.getSessionsByBinding(...)` (`services/relay/notify-target.ts:98-115`) to find the most recently active chat. Bridged bindings vacate `sessionMap` (§7.2, task 1.11), so task-completion notices and `relay_notify_user` would silently stop reaching a bridged chat.

So: **a live bridge counts as an active chat.** `pickMostRecentChat` also considers bridge rows, each contributing `{ binding, chatId, at: bridge.lastActivityAt }`, where `lastActivityAt` is stamped by `ingest` (task 1.6) and by successful delivery (task 1.8). Recency competes on ONE axis across both sources; ties resolve to the existing behaviour so no unbridged case changes.

The resulting proactive send still goes through the consent gate as an INITIATE (task 1.7's classification rule — a scheduled or proactive message has no inbound cascade root), so `canInitiate` remains the switch it always was. Do not add a bypass.

Tests:
- A7.5: with every session vacated from `sessionMap`, `resolveNotifyTarget` still resolves the bridged chat, and its send is gated as an initiate (assert the `relay.bridge.initiate.…` principal on the publish).
- A mixed case: one unbridged binding with a recent session and one bridged binding with a more recent `lastActivityAt` — the bridged chat wins; reverse the recency and the unbridged one wins.
- A tie resolves exactly as today.
- Consent table cases 5 and 6 (scheduled task with `canInitiate` on/off) exercised through this path end to end.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Carry visibility, formatting guidance, and topic labels in room_context
tasks.description:
Implements spec §8 (privacy-mode honesty, the `room_context` half), §15 (message formatting across the boundary), §5.6 / §9.2 (the sanitized topic label). Acceptance criteria: A8.4, the render half of A5.10, A9.3, and the §13 markdown-table integration case.

Three additions to the structured context built by `buildRoomContext` (`services/rooms/room-context.ts:140`) and rendered by `formatRoomContext` (`services/runtimes/shared/room-context-block.ts:522`), which all three runtimes call. No runtime knows a room is bridged; framing stays structured context (ADR-0273) through the one shared builder.

1. **`visibility: 'partial' | 'full'` with the reason.** Sourced from the bridge row's `visibility`, which is recorded from Telegram's `getMe().can_read_all_group_messages` (task 1.2) with `visibilityCheckedAt`. A model that believes it saw a whole conversation it saw a tenth of will confidently describe a group it cannot read. FLAG FOR EXECUTE: the spec fixes the source but not the refresh cadence for `visibilityCheckedAt` — refresh on bridge create and on adapter start, and treat a stale value as `partial` (the conservative direction), unless EXECUTE finds a cheaper live read.

2. **Platform formatting rules and `maxLength`** for turns in a bridged room. This is the same information the adapter already puts on the inbound payload as `responseContext.formattingInstructions` (`inbound.ts:460-465`), now made available to a turn triggered by a ROOM rather than by an envelope. It is GUIDANCE, it lives in the labels region, and it is NOT load-bearing: the outbound adapter remains the enforcement backstop, unchanged, and it already owns splitting and escaping. Guidance without a backstop is a prompt pretending to be a mechanism; a backstop without guidance produces mangled tables that were avoidable.

3. **The sanitized forum-topic label**, rendered per entry OUTSIDE the fence from the external ref's `threadName` (task 1.1's column, populated by task 1.6). It is a label, not a message, so it passes `sanitizeIdentity` from `@dorkos/shared/untrusted-text` — the existing function, never a second copy — at write time as well as render time. Phase 1 folds all topics into one room (D-6 Q1: defer the split until Slack's `thread_ts` is in hand so the choice is made once), and without the label a folded room is an unreadable interleaving of several conversations, which would make the room log worse evidence than the chat it projects.

Do not change the fence, the nonce, or the region boundaries — task 1.4 owns `authorOrigin` and the standing line; this task adds labels beside them.

Tests:
- A8.4: `room_context` for a turn in a partially visible bridged group carries `visibility: 'partial'`.
- A5.10 (render half): a forum-topic entry renders its sanitized topic label outside the fence.
- A9.3: a forum topic name containing markup is sanitized in the store, not only at render.
- §13 integration: a room post containing a markdown table is delivered to Telegram without breaking, pinning BOTH halves of §15 — the guidance in context and the adapter backstop.

This is the phase-1 entry point AND the fallback that keeps this whole spec unblocked if DOR-856's claim card slips (§2.3): the claim-card primary action is task 2.1, but a person can always bridge from here.

In the client (`apps/client/src/layers/…`, Feature-Sliced Design, barrel imports only), on the Connections › Messaging binding detail sheet:

4. **`sessionStrategy` is hidden for a bridged binding**, replaced by one line explaining that a bridged chat keeps its history in the channel.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Show the visibility badge and external-origin marks on a bridged channel
tasks.description:
Implements spec §8 (the badge half), §4.3 (origin marks), §3.4's platform-title subtitle. Acceptance criteria: A8.1, A8.2, A8.3.

1. **The visibility badge** in a bridged group channel's header: **"sees mentions only"** or **"sees everything"**, sourced from the bridge row's `visibility`, which comes from Telegram's `getMe` — NOT from config. Tapping it explains that this is Telegram's own switch and that changing it means removing and re-adding the bot. It is not a setting, and it must not render as one.
   The expanded copy states both honest gaps: (a) `can_read_all_group_messages` is BOT-WIDE, not per-group — a bot with privacy off that was added to a group before the flag changed may still be restricted there, so the copy says "in groups where it was added after this was set"; inferring per-group visibility from observed traffic would be a guess presented as a fact. (b) The badge describes Telegram's gate ONLY; the adapter's own `respondMode` is a SECOND gate, and a bot with privacy off but `respondMode: 'thread-aware'` still sees only addressed messages. A person reading "sees everything" next to a log of only mentions would rightly conclude the product is lying.
2. **A bridged DM shows no badge.** Privacy mode is a group concept; a badge there would imply a limit that does not exist. (If task 1.3 took the D-6 Q2 fallback and bridged private chats are kind `channel`, key this on `platformChatType`, not on room kind.)
3. **Origin marks** — the platform icon plus its name, e.g. "Miguel · Telegram" — on every external member in the roster, in the room sheet, and BESIDE EACH OF THEIR ENTRIES. Rendered from the `origin` field task 1.4 puts on `RoomRosterEntry` (derived from the stored natural key), never re-derived in the client. This is the difference between "a person on this machine wrote this" and "a stranger on the internet wrote this", which §9 makes a security boundary — so it must be legible at a glance, not a tooltip.
4. **The platform chat title as a subtitle** on the room sheet, so a platform title change (which deliberately does NOT rename the room — `room-service.ts:317-321`) never silently diverges from the room's title.

Calm Tech design language; works on mobile, tablet, and desktop; every element justifies its existence. NOTE: the claim-card surfaces are DOR-856's (Language & IA project) — cross-reference them, do not rebuild them here.

Tests:
- A8.1: a bridged group room's header shows a visibility badge sourced from `getMe`, not from config.
- A8.2: a bridged DM room shows no badge.
- A8.3: the badge's explanation names Telegram as the owner of the switch, describes the re-add ritual, and names `respondMode` as the second gate.
- Origin marks render for an external member and NOT for the operator, an agent, or the system voice.
- Client tests via mock `Transport`; add the Dev Playground showcase if the badge or origin mark is a reusable component.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P1] Add the bridged-room security suite as its own file
tasks.description:
Implements spec §9 (security: untrusted authorship and the injection stance, DOR-633) and §13's security bullet. Acceptance criteria: A9.1, A9.2, A9.6, and the standing-line and laundering assertions that back A9.4 and A9.5.

This suite gets its own file BECAUSE §9 is the section most likely to rot — the mechanisms it pins are spread across the author registry, the roster, the context builder, and the fence, and no single feature test would notice all of them regressing.

The stance being pinned: **untrusted is a property of the AUTHOR, established at write time, carried on the entry, and enforced at render. It is never inferred from the text and never re-derived at render time.**

Tests:
- **Fence integrity with a hostile external body**, asserted on `formatRoomContext`'s output (which all three runtimes call): a message containing a forged fence-closing marker, a `<room_context>` tag, and a newline-plus-marker each render INSIDE the fence with the nonce intact (A9.1).
- **Preamble free of `<` and `>`** for a hostile display name, a hostile platform chat title, and a hostile forum topic name, including NEL, zero-width, and angle-bracket variants; the preamble contains no `<` or `>` at all (A9.2). Every one of these goes through `sanitizeIdentity` from `@dorkos/shared/untrusted-text` — assert the existing function is the one used, so a second copy cannot appear later.
- **`ownRecent` laundering with tags defused** (A9.5): external text quoted back by the agent lands in `ownRecent`, which remains OUTSIDE the fence and remains the documented laundering path (`room-context-block.ts:52-66`, measured at 46 characters ahead of the fence). `defuseSystemTags` on that region is load-bearing for exactly this feature; the test uses a genuine external author, not a synthetic string.
- **`permissionMode: 'default'` on every bridge-created binding** (A9.6), and no bridge path writes a more permissive mode — assert by enumerating bridge write paths, not by checking one.
- **The structural levers of §9.3**, one test each, phrased as what a stranger cannot reach: cannot make an agent run at all (only a claimed chat routes anywhere; in a group only an addressed message survives privacy mode + `shouldProcessGroupMessage` + `mention-only`); cannot make an agent run repeatedly (turn budget's two ceilings, cascade guard, ingest ceiling); cannot speak to a chat the operator never connected (A9.7 — asserted through `deliver`'s author check AND, independently, through the route guard); cannot start a conversation on any channel (`canInitiate` defaults false, cross-room laundering closed); cannot get an agent added to a room (`addMember` is operator-only, `room-service.ts:588-590`); cannot impersonate the operator or another agent (author identity is server-derived, display name is a sanitized label).
- **A3.1** (belongs here because it is the consent floor): an inbound message from an UNCLAIMED chat creates no room, no author, no entry, and runs no turn — asserted on the store.
- **§9.5**: nothing about the bot token, adapter config, or agent credentials enters a room entry or a room context.

What we are NOT claiming, and the tests must not pretend otherwise: this is not injection-proof. A model that reads a stranger's message and acts on it can still do harm within granted permissions. The permission mode is the real bound.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P2] Add "Answer in a channel" as the claim card's primary action
tasks.description:
Implements spec §3.1's first entry point and §12's phase 2. Founder rationale: `design-decisions.md` D-1 Move 2 and D-3.

**BLOCKED ON DOR-856.** The claim feed backend, the chat claim as a first-class act, one-chat-one-agent uniqueness with the explicit move dialog, atomic adapter+binding creation in the wizard, and `BindingStore.resolve` filtering `enabled` are Move 2's outputs and ship in the Language & IA project. This task CONSUMES them; it does not rebuild them, and the claim card component itself is DOR-856's. Do not duplicate that scope — extend it.

What this task adds:
1. **"Answer in a channel"** as the claim card's PRIMARY action, creating chat claim + binding + bridge + room ATOMICALLY — one path, the same one task 1.3 and 1.14 already use, so there is no second create path to keep honest. The secondary action, "Answer privately", stays today's session-per-chat behaviour with no room.
2. Until a chat is claimed there is no room, no author row for the stranger, no entry, and no agent run. **An unclaimed chat NEVER triggers an agent** — no model run, no spend, no prompt-injection surface. A stranger's message renders as data on a cockpit claim card only; the bot stays silent in-chat until the chat is claimed, deliberately quieter than Claude Code Channels' pairing-code pattern, which requires the bot to answer an unknown sender with a code.
3. Claim cards collapse per chat: `Ignore` mutes the chat; `Block` drops its future traffic without a card. (If DOR-856 already ships this collapse behaviour, verify it and cross-reference; do not reimplement.)

Tests: the atomic create path leaves either all four artifacts or none; an unclaimed chat's inbound produces no room, author, entry, or turn (shares the A3.1 assertion with task 1.16); the primary action lands the person in the new channel; Ignore and Block behave distinctly.

tasks.subject: [chats-as-channels] [P2] Add the group-add claim flow
tasks.description:
Implements spec §12's phase 2 group-add flow. Founder rationale: `design-decisions.md` D-3 items 4, 6, and 7.

**BLOCKED ON DOR-856** for the same reasons as task 2.1 — it extends Move 2's claim surface.

A bot added to a group is a NEW group-kind chat and goes through the same claim flow: "added to 'X' by Ana — which agent should join? / Ignore / Leave". Leave is a real action, not a dismissal.

On claim-with-bridge, the room is created by task 1.3's path, which means: room kind `channel`, the bound agent `mention-only` AT EVERY OBSERVABLE POINT (over-participation, not silence, is the failure mode users complain about — `meta/agent-etiquette.md`), the title sanitized from the platform chat title, and the visibility badge stating what the bot can see (task 1.15).

Telegram privacy mode stays default-ON, so a bridged group channel's room log contains only what the bot legitimately received. Turning it off remains Telegram's own deliberate remove-and-re-add ritual — DorkOS never flips it and never offers to. Nothing in this flow may offer it.

A broadcast channel is refused: the card offers only "Ignore"/"Leave" (task 1.3 enforces the refusal server-side; this surfaces it honestly).

Tests: a group-add event produces one claim card naming the adder and the group; claiming with bridge creates a `channel` room whose agent is `mention-only`; Leave calls the platform's leave and writes no room; a broadcast-channel add offers only Ignore and Leave.
